Project Brain

An AI-powered project memory platform designed for team collaboration and actionable task intelligence — eliminating institutional amnesia at scale.

01 — Challenge

The Problem: Institutional Amnesia

Modern teams suffer from context loss — decisions, milestones, and project updates scatter across tools, leaving new members and distributed teams perpetually behind. The strategic goal was to shift away from manual documentation by building a living, searchable, AI-powered memory that automatically surfaces context.

"Modern teams suffer from context loss — decisions, milestones, and project updates scatter across tools, leaving new members and distributed teams perpetually behind."

The design strategy required establishing a delicate AI-human interaction model that prioritizes user trust, particularly regarding knowledge retrieval and ingestion.

02 — Research & Discovery

Grounding Design in Real Friction

The UX process was grounded in understanding friction points of modern knowledge work through a multi-method approach.

Contextual Interviews Competitive Analysis Task Analysis Rapid Concept Testing Low-fi Wireframes

Competitors analyzed: Notion, Linear, Confluence. Key behavioral pain points surfaced:

Critical decisions buried in chat or email threads, completely inaccessible.
Onboarding new team members took weeks before reaching full productivity.
Users showed low trust in AI suggestions without original source context.
Meeting notes were rarely translated into actionable items.
03 — UX Architecture

Systems Thinking Over Isolated Features

The product architecture demonstrates a systems-thinking approach where individual features — Brain, Chat, Memory — feed into a cohesive mental model rather than acting as isolated tools.

Feature User Goal Design Decision
Smart Onboarding Productive from day one Automated brief template with progressive disclosure; highlights "Smart Onboarding" on login.
Memory Timeline Audit decisions & milestones Chronological entry system with filter taxonomy; searchable log with AI-summarized insights.
AI Brain / Ingestion Never re-explain context Intuitive upload UX flow supporting PDF, DOCX, TXT, MD (up to 20MB) + Drive, GitHub, Notion, Jira integrations.
AI Chat Q&A Instant answers from docs Conversational UI with source-linking trust pattern and contextual prompt starters + voice commands.
Workspace Dashboard Proactive task awareness Notification hierarchy with AI trust signaling; centralizes calendar, quick actions, AI-suggested events.
Project Boards Visual workflow tracking Kanban-first layout with status taxonomy to visualize and track tasks.
04 — Paper Wireframe

From Sketch to Structure

Before any pixel was pushed to Figma, the core layouts were validated through rapid paper wireframes — prioritising information hierarchy and user flow over visual polish. The sketches explored two critical surfaces: the mobile project sidebar and the desktop workspace dashboard.

Screen A
Mobile Project Sidebar
A collapsible sidebar prioritises project switching and account context (Maverick 2.0), with a clear logout and manage-projects anchor at the bottom — reducing navigation depth on small screens.
Screen B
Dashboard — Workspace Overview
The desktop layout uses a three-column information hierarchy: Calendar (time anchoring), Quick Actions (task focus), and AI Suggested Events — directly addressing the cognitive load pain points uncovered in research.
Pattern
AI Trust Signalling
The “AI is analysing your project…” placeholder and the Open AI Brain CTA were sketched at the wireframe stage — establishing trust transparency as a first-class design primitive, not an afterthought.
Detail
Upload Docs Panel
A dedicated drag-and-drop upload zone (PDF, DOCX, TXT, MD — up to 20MB) was sketched within Quick Actions, mapping directly to the AI ingestion flow identified in the UX architecture phase.
Navigation
Global Action Bar
Search, Invite Member, notifications, and profile are persistent in the top bar — ensuring collaboration and context retrieval are always one tap away regardless of current view state.
Insight
Sketching as Alignment
Paper wireframes were shared with 4 stakeholders before Figma work began. 3 layout iterations were resolved in a single session — validating the low-fi approach as a faster alignment tool than screen-based prototypes.
05 — Visual Design

Calm Authority — Reducing Cognitive Load

The UI balances an impressive aesthetic with functional legibility. The visual tone was defined as "Calm Authority" — deep navy and midnight darks assert focus, while teal-green accents signal AI intelligence.

Midnight
Deep Navy
Teal AI
White
Surface

A contextual dual-mode system was implemented — dark mode for marketing/onboarding to generate excitement, light mode for the core productivity app. The Figma component library followed an atomic design system, with rapid 3-day sprint cycles from concept to lo-fi to testing. Accessibility audits were conducted at every major milestone.

05 — Impact & Results

Measurable ROI of Design Decisions

Success backed by strong validation metrics — not assumptions.

3×
Faster onboarding for new team members compared to the previous baseline.
41→19s
Context retrieval time slashed from 41 seconds down to 19 seconds.
40%
Reduction in perceived mental effort confirmed through user testing sessions.
87%
Task completion rate achieved on the first-use prototype.
Strategic Verdict

Project Brain succeeds because it addresses the foundational barrier to AI adoption in knowledge work: trust. By proactively designing source-linking and confidence signaling into the AI surfaces, the design effectively bridges the gap between machine intelligence and human usability.

SecondHome

A calm, neutral co-parenting hub that transforms scattered logistics — schedules, expenses, child profiles — into one shared, friction-free space for separated families.

Project Timeline
01 — Project Overview

The Co-Parenting Logistics & Communication Hub

Divorced and separated parents constantly struggle with the fragmented logistics of co-parenting. Crucial information is routinely scattered across chaotic text threads, missed emails, and un-synced digital calendars. SecondHome is a mobile platform engineered to eliminate this friction. By centralising custody schedules, shared expenses, and vital child data, SecondHome replaces clinical, stressful legacy software with a calm, objective, and user-centred management ecosystem.

Role: Lead UX Designer & Systems Strategist
Timeline: 6 Weeks
Tools: Figma, Framer, Pen & Paper
02 — Discovery & Research

Framing the Problem Space

The project began by framing the emotional and practical complexities of co-parenting through foundational research questions aimed at minimising behavioural friction:

What are the primary triggers for communication breakdowns between co-parents?
How do parents currently track shared expenses and scheduling changes?
What psychological barriers exist when using traditional, legally-focused co-parenting apps?
How can the interface remain neutral and prevent escalations during disagreements?
03 — Empathy Mapping

Understanding the Emotional Reality

To map the day-to-day realities of separated parents, an Empathy Map was developed to analyse current user behaviour — capturing what they say, think, do, and feel in the co-parenting context.

Says/Thinks: "I hate asking my ex for money." "Did they remember it's picture day?" "The current apps feel like I'm filling out legal paperwork."
Does: Scrolls through weeks of texts to find a clothing size; manually calculates split expenses; uses screenshots as "proof" of agreements.
Feels: Anxious before opening notifications, overwhelmed by logistical overhead, guilty about how parental stress affects the children, defensive during negotiations.
04 — Target Audience & Personas

Two Distinct User Archetypes

Based on qualitative research, two distinct user archetypes were defined to guide the app's information architecture — representing opposite ends of the organisational spectrum.

📋
Marcus
The Planner
"As a meticulously organised dad, I want a single, immutable source of truth for my kids' schedules and expenses so that I can eliminate logistical guesswork and co-parent peacefully."
Profile
  • 38, Project Manager
  • Father of two · 50% custody
Frustrations
  • Unpredictable last-minute schedule changes
  • Tracking split costs for soccer & camp
🎨
Sarah
The Disorganised Parent
"As a busy, non-linear thinker, I need to access my kids' real-time needs and request schedule shifts instantly on the go, without feeling judged or penalised by a clunky interface."
Profile
  • 35, Freelance Designer
  • Mother of two · constantly on the move
Frustrations
  • Forgets to update the shared Google calendar
  • Can't recall kids' sizes while shopping
05 — User Journey & Pain Points

Marcus's Journey Through a Schedule Conflict

Mapping Marcus's journey through a typical schedule conflict revealed severe friction points in traditional communication models — from identifying a conflict to the eventual missed event.

"The journey exposed four compounding failure modes — stress, anxiety, hostility, and missed events — each made worse by unstructured text-based communication."

Three strategic opportunities emerged: an Automated Trade Workflow to replace text negotiations, Micro-Information Delivery for high-stress on-the-go moments, and an Objective Expense Splitting system to remove personal bias from financial transactions.

06 — Ideation & Wireframing

Paper Wireframes — Layout Thinking

Transitioning from research to visual layout required low-fidelity sketching focused on de-escalating user tension through clean content hierarchy. The dashboard structure prioritised the immediate daily schedule and active swap requests at top, followed by Kid Profiles and the Shared Ledger.

Dashboard Structure: Immediate daily schedule and active "Swap Requests" prioritised at top, followed by Kid Profiles and Shared Ledger.
UI Tone Strategy: Stripped away aggressive notification badges in favour of soft, neutral tones — mutes, sages, and cool grays — to actively lower psychological friction.
Workflow Drafts: Step-by-step wizard for schedule swaps, requiring a counter-date proposal up front to keep interactions solution-oriented.
07 — Low-Fidelity Prototype

Refining the Design — Prototype v2.0

The low-fidelity prototype connected all core flows — dashboard through the calendar's swap request system, kid profiles, and expense ledger — establishing full interaction logic before applying visual design.

08 — Feature Deep Dive

The Dynamic Custody Calendar & Swap Workflow

The most complex feature — the custody swap system — was mapped as a full user flow to ensure both parents experience a structured, emotion-free negotiation. Parent A initiates a request, a neutral conflict check occurs, and Parent B can Accept, Decline, or Counter without a single text message exchanged.

Visual Clarity: Soft, distinct colour blocks represent each parent's custody days — readable at a single glance.
Friction-Free Swapping: Swap Request prompts Parent A to offer a reciprocal day. Parent B receives a neutral notification to Accept, Decline, or Counter.
No Emotional Baggage: No text messages, no interpretation issues — just a clean database update upon mutual consent.
09 — High-Fidelity UI

Refining the Design — Final Visual Language

The final high-fidelity interface translates complex interpersonal systems into an objective, calming mobile experience. The purple-forward palette paired with clean typography brings calm authority without aggression — every colour choice tested against emotional resonance for users in high-stress parenting moments.

The Dynamic Custody Calendar: Soft colour blocks per parent, swap request wizard keeps all negotiation structured and solution-oriented.
The Kid Profile — Single Source of Truth: Scannable card layouts for on-the-go moments — clothing sizes with timestamps, medical logs, tap-to-copy teacher contacts.
The Shared Expense Ledger: Transparent math, no accusatory language. Receipt uploads, auto-extracted totals, and "Approve to Split" notifications remove direct financial confrontation.
Key Takeaway

SecondHome successfully shifts the co-parenting paradigm from an emotional battleground to an objective logistical partnership. By designing for neutral ground — structured forms instead of freeform texts, shared ledgers instead of disputed memories, collaborative swap flows instead of combative negotiations — the product transforms co-parenting logistics from a source of conflict into a quiet, reliable system that both parents can trust. The kids never had to know there was a problem.

Design Execution

High-fidelity interface system

The final interface system focused on emotional clarity, fast navigation, and low-friction coordination between co-parents. Every screen was designed to reduce ambiguity during scheduling, approvals, and financial communication while keeping the experience calm and approachable.

UX Architecture

Wireframes & information hierarchy

Before visual refinement, the product structure was mapped through detailed wireflows and low-fidelity exploration. This helped validate navigation logic, custody flows, profile management, expense handling, and notification pathways across the entire experience.

The Story
Where I Started
Overweight, low energy, low confidence. I wasn't living — I was existing. The gym felt like a foreign place, food felt like the enemy, and motivation felt like something other people had. I was the guy who started on Monday and quit by Wednesday.
The Shift
No crash diets. No magic supplement. Just showing up consistently — even on bad days. I tracked every lift on Hevy, learned progressive overload, fixed my sleep, and started eating with intention. The results followed the habits, not the other way around.
Mind Over Everything
The hardest reps are the ones you do when nobody is watching. I learned that discipline is a skill, not a personality trait. You build it like a muscle — slowly, with resistance, and it gets stronger every time you don't quit.
Where I Am Now
I feel genuinely better — more energy, sharper focus, more confidence in everything I do. The body transformation was the side effect. The real prize was proving to myself that I can do hard things. That belief changed my career, my design work, everything.
